memory_candidates.content: When mechanically inserting a new numbered list item into markdown files at scale (e.g. via a script that finds 'the last numbered item before section X'), a wrapped/multi-line list item (text continuing on an indented next line with no leading digit) can cause the insertion to land between the item's first line and its own continuation, silently splitting it. Always add a post-hoc structural verification pass (regex-check for an indented, non-numbered line immediately following each inserted line) rather than trusting the mechanical pass alone, especially across a large batch (20+ files) where manual review of every file is impractical.

For a postflight-style gate script that must decide whether an absent artifact is 'expected but missing' (a defect) vs. 'never produced by design' (not a defect), prefer deriving the expectation from the calling context/dispatch shape itself (e.g. whether the caller supplied a handoff_path) over maintaining a hardcoded allowlist of agent names. An allowlist drifts behind the agent roster as new agents are added; a dispatch-derived default (with an explicit opt-out flag for the rare exception) is self-maintaining and fails toward detection rather than silent excusal.
